thread:
jamal: heads up — acme reported a bunch of 429s right after last night's rate-policy rollout in us-west. they say it started ~02:15 UTC and they also saw billing-metering spikes. anyone already on this?

alex: seeing alerts for a surge of 429s from a few heavy api keys. pattern looks like burst -> quota exhaustion rather than auth failing.

maria: confirmed in logs: policy v2.3.1 applied at 02:10, canary=20% but some customers got full rollout due to routing bug. reproducing now with their key.

sophie: yikes. can you paste the exact error body from the API? acme included a stacktrace in the ticket but truncated.

jamal: their client got this: `{\n  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",\n  "retry_after": 30,\n  "scope": "account"\n}` — but some requests show `401` for a few mins, likely collateral from the retry storm.

support-bot: ticket #4532 updated: customer provided cURL repro and timestamps. attached request headers include `x-rate-policy: v2.3.1` and `x-client-region: us-west-2`.

alex: repro steps from acme (sanitized): `for i in {1..1000}; do curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate; done` — they didn't space requests. yields quick quota drain.

maria: two things: 1) routing bug allowed a subset of keys to skip canary; 2) a metrics aggregation bug under-reported per-key token counts, so policy engine underestimated usage for bursts. both together meant some keys hit full limits fast.

sophie: any customer impact on tokens charged? their finance team is asking.

jamal: preliminary billing logs show tokens logged as consumed — we didn't double-bill but some requests failed after being charged because they hit limit mid-stream. need legal/product to advise.

alex: immediate mitigations: pause rollout for v2.3.1 (stop push), re-enable prefix K/V cache for affected model, and add a temporary smoothing throttle (small token-per-second cap) for keys that hit sudden exhausiton.

maria: I can push a rollback of the policy rollout flag in 2 mins. deploy-bot: `rollout-ctl revert --policy v2.3.1 --target canary` queued.

deploy-bot: rollback started at 2001203510. will take ~3 minutes to fully re-evaluate routing.

sophie: I've flagged the customer for a billing hold and added a note to CS: don't charge for failed requests until we have final reconciled numbers.

jamal: ops follow-up: need an incident postmortem with timeline and the fix for the routing check. Maria — can you add the metric that was under-reporting to the alerting set? we should trigger before canary flips.

maria: on it. I'll add a new alert for per-key token delta vs observed upstream delta (threshold 300% over 1m). also adding a canary-traffic-consistency check.

alex: long-term: add graceful degradation path — if policy engine sees a sudden burst, respond with progressive 202 (enqueue) or lower-rate 429 with longer retry_after to avoid retry storms.

support-bot: updated ticket #4532 with rollback status and CS notes. customer acknowledged and asked for ETA on fix.

jamal: once rollback is done, do a controlled re-rollout only after we ship the routing patch + new alerting. no more overnight flips until we have automatic consistency checks. :thumbsup:

maria: rollback finished at 2001203540, metrics starting to normalize. I'll follow up with a small canary re-run at 10% only after the patch merges.

sophie: I'll schedule a sync with ACME for 10:30 PST and share logs + compensation plan.

jamal: thanks all. we'll draft a short postmortem template and assign owners. closing this thread for now but leave the ticket open for billing reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
